acceptance_criteria.criterion: Commands are grouped by category in output
Commands with hidden: true are excluded from help output
Commands with helpHidden: true are excluded from help output
helpVariants are rendered as indented sub-entries
Commands with helpOrder sort numerically; unordered commands retain insertion order
help entry always appears last regardless of helpOrder

summary: Implemented src/help.ts with printHelp(commands, config): filters hidden/helpHidden commands, stable-sorts by helpOrder (undefined → Infinity), groups by category with bold headers, renders helpVariants as sub-entries, and always appends a synthetic help entry last.

Created tests/help.test.ts with 19 tests covering all 7 acceptance criteria: category grouping, hidden/helpHidden filtering, helpVariants rendering, helpOrder sort, insertion-order preservation, and help-always-last guarantee.
Fixed a test pattern issue — initial search for '  test\n' didn't match because command lines include padding before the description. Changed to '  test ' which matches the padded format.
All 94 tests pass (19 new + 75 prior). npm run typecheck clean.

comments.note: src/help.ts formatEntry() uses padEnd(28) for the command name column. If a command id or helpVariant string exceeds 28 characters, the description column will not be visually aligned. A max-width or truncation guard could be added to keep the output clean for long command names (e.g., commands with subcommand paths). Deferred to Phase B when real command shapes are known.

The resolveVersion() helper in src/help.ts duplicates logic that will likely appear again in createMenu() (Phase B). Once Phase B introduces the menu engine, consider extracting resolveVersion() to a shared location (e.g., src/utils.ts or exported from src/index.ts) to avoid duplication.

Unordered commands in printHelp() are sorted last (helpOrder ?? Infinity). This is the simplest stable-sort implementation, but it means ordered and unordered commands cannot interleave — all ordered commands precede all unordered within a category. If Phase B needs exact interleaving (e.g., 2 ordered, 1 unordered between them), the sort strategy will need revision.

summary: All 7 ACs verified. Code review + 19 new tests confirm: category grouping via Set over sorted commands (correct display order), hidden/helpHidden filtering via single filter call, helpVariants rendered inline after parent via tuple iterator, stable sort (helpOrder ?? Infinity) preserves insertion order of unordered commands, synthetic help entry appended unconditionally after all category loops.
94/94 tests pass (19 new + 75 prior). npm run typecheck exits 0. No regressions.

comments.note: If a caller registers a Command with id: 'help', printHelp() will emit that command line AND the synthetic help entry — resulting in two 'help' lines in the output. The API has no guard against this collision. A defensive check (filter id === 'help' from user commands, or skip the synthetic entry if a help command is already present) could be added when the public API is stabilised in Phase B.
No observations beyond the duplicate-id edge case above — implementation is clean, well-structured, and tests are thorough.

comments.note: Fix-Forward: replaced workspaceRoot: '/tmp/test' with workspaceRoot: process.cwd() in the makeConfig() helper in tests/help.test.ts. The AGENTS.md cross-platform policy prohibits hardcoded Unix paths in test fixtures. printHelp() never reads workspaceRoot, so this is a zero-behavior change — the fix satisfies the cross-platform rule without affecting any assertion.

The usage string in printHelp() is hardcoded to 'Usage: node scripts/cli.js [command] [options]'. This is specific to this workspace's invocation pattern. If the library is used in a project with a different entry point name, the usage line will be incorrect. Phase B should consider adding a usageLine or invocationName field to MenuConfig (or defaulting to process.argv[1]) to make the usage string reflect the actual invocation.

resolveVersion() is a private helper in src/help.ts that duplicates logic likely to appear in createMenu() (Phase B). The Developer flagged this. In Phase B, consider extracting it to src/utils.ts or exporting it from src/index.ts to avoid duplication. It is correctly scoped as private for now.

Category display order is derived implicitly via [...new Set(sorted.map(c => c.category))]. The comment 'Derive category display order from first appearance in the sorted list' documents this correctly. Note for Phase B: if explicit category ordering is needed (e.g., via a categoryOrder field in MenuConfig), this Set approach will need to be replaced.

[documentation-forward] The usage line in printHelp() is hardcoded to 'node scripts/cli.js [command] [options]'. API docs should note this is intentional for Phase A and that a configurable usageLine or invocationName is deferred to Phase B when MenuConfig is finalized.

No blocking issues. Implementation is clean, well-structured, and consistently idiomatic. The Set-based category ordering from the sorted command list is a clean one-liner.
